hardware_evidence_vocabulary.NOT_RUN: no hardware capture of this row's cases exists; the default for any row that sets no field
hardware_evidence_vocabulary.CAPTURED: a hardware capture exists but was not acceptance-eligible, so it establishes nothing about PSP behaviour

tests.measurement_note: Measured by the 2026-10-15 PSP-3000 single-case run (firmware 6.6.1) of public commit b5d6fc5b, case hle-vtimer-unit: 13 records and the done record, all PASS, acceptance-eligible with 0 blockers. Cited: CreateVTimer returned a UID, StartVTimer returned 0, sceKernelDelayThread(20000) returned 0, StopVTimer on the running timer returned 1, and DeleteVTimer on the stopped timer returned 0. While the timer ran, GetVTimerBase and ReferVTimerStatus each returned 0 and gave the same 64-bit base, whose high word equals the system clock's; after StopVTimer both returned 0 and the base read 0. GetVTimerTime read 38,316 and 242,695 either side of the 20 ms delay, a delta of 204,379, while sceKernelGetSystemTimeWide advanced 220,608 between its two reads. The probe's host0 record writes offset the two intervals, so the deltas agree only within about 8%: this is consistent with the system clock's microsecond unit and is not a precise rate measurement. At both reads the base plus the VTimer time stayed below the next system-clock read, which is consistent with time = system time - base and base = the system time at Start; no system-clock reading was taken at Start itself. Absolute system-clock values are not cited.
tests.invariant: one VTimer: start, a VTimer and a system clock reading either side of one bounded 20 ms delay, the VTimer base and Refer base field while running and after stop, then stop and delete; each 64-bit clock is recorded as low and high words
tests.risk: low; one probe-owned VTimer, a bounded 20 ms wait, deleted in the case
tests.reset: one PRX launch; PSPLink soft reset before the next launch

tests.evidence_note: Captured incomplete by the 2026-10-15 PSP-3000 single-case run (firmware 6.6.1) of public commit b5d6fc5b, case hle-null-out-pointers, the last case of the session. null-vtimer-create was recorded PASS. The stream then stopped after the step marker null-sys-status, which the probe writes just before its first NULL call (sceKernelReferSystemStatus(NULL)), 0.9 s after launch; no record for that cell or any later one arrived. No completion arrived within the 240 s case timeout, the module was not proven unloaded, and the console needed a power cycle. The capture itself is not acceptance-eligible and establishes nothing about PSP behaviour: it does not show whether that call faulted, hung or would have returned. Maintainer retirement: the kernel pointer check rejects kernel-space addresses but not address 0, so ReferSystemStatus(NULL) writes through NULL and faults; the VTimer getters also write through their out pointers. No game can rely on these results. The probe was a single launch, not in the campaign queue; it is retired and never to be scheduled.
tests.invariant: Retired and never to be scheduled: ReferSystemStatus(NULL) writes through address 0 and faults; the VTimer getters also write through their mandatory out pointers. Preserve the CAPTURED run only; no game can rely on these results.
tests.risk: high: retired and never to be scheduled; PSP-3000 hangs on the first call, sceKernelReferSystemStatus(NULL), because address 0 is not rejected by the kernel pointer check and the call writes through NULL.
tests.reset: one PRX launch; PSPLink soft reset before the next launch

tests.measurement_note: Measured by the 2026-10-15 PSP-3000 single-case re-run (firmware 6.6.1) of public commit 7fc1641e, case hle-audio-src: 17 records and the done record, all PASS, acceptance-eligible with 0 blockers. The first run, of 22b027f6, recorded the same words in the other 16 records, but its two final-cleanup cells were SKIP, so that envelope was not acceptance-eligible and is not cited. Cited: with nothing reserved, SRCChRelease and SRCOutputBlocking (one silent 1024-sample stereo block at the maximum volume) each returned 0x80260008. SRCChReserve(1024, 44100, 2) returned 0, an identical second reserve returned 0x80268002, and SRCOutputBlocking then returned 0x400, the sample count. SRCChRelease returned 0, and a second release returned 0x80260008. With nothing reserved, a sample count of 0 returned 0x80000104, and 65 and 4096 samples were accepted; 48000 Hz was accepted; 1 channel returned 0x80000104 and 4 channels returned 0x80000003. Each accepted shape was released at once (0). Output2Reserve(512) then SRCChReserve returned 0x80268002, and SRCChReserve then Output2Reserve(512) returned 0x80268002, each with the first reservation released afterwards (0); nothing was left reserved. Not cited: the upper sample-count bound, frequencies other than 44100 and 48000, channel counts other than 1, 2 and 4, volume validation, releasing one reservation through the other API, and the audible output (silence).
tests.invariant: Unreserved SRC release and silent output; one 1024-sample, 44100 Hz, stereo reservation, a second reserve and one silent blocking output; release after the blocking drain and release again; six single-field invalid reserve shapes, with immediate release on any unexpected success; Output2-then-SRC and SRC-then-Output2 reservations, with both resources released. The project NID corpus has no SRC rest-sample query.

tests.measurement_note: Measured by the 2026-10-15 PSP-3000 single-case run (firmware 6.6.1) of public commit 22b027f6, the pre-merge head of the change that added this probe (its hle-timer-order source is unchanged in the merged commit 7fc1641e), case hle-timer-order: 17 records and the done record, all PASS, acceptance-eligible with 0 blockers. Cited: each SetAlarm returned a UID, and SetVTimerHandler and StartVTimer returned 0. The callbacks ran in this order: the first-set 50000 us alarm, then the second-set 50000 us alarm 17,125 us later in system time; the 30000 us alarm, then the 100000 us alarm set before it, 53,561 us later; the VTimer handler (due 60000 us after Start), then the 60000 us alarm 13,579 us later; and the SetAlarm(0) handler had run by the end of a 100000 us wait. Each pair was set with a host0 step record between the two calls, so the due times were not equal and the cells do not measure a tie-break at equal due time, and the SetAlarm(0) cell takes no set-time reading. After their handlers returned 0, CancelAlarm on each of the six alarm UIDs returned 0x8002019F; StopVTimer of the still-running timer returned 1 and DeleteVTimer returned 0. No absolute delay is cited.
tests.invariant: Shared callback sequence and system-time low/high words for two same-delay alarms set A then B, a longer alarm set before a shorter one, a nominally equal VTimer/alarm due pair, and SetAlarm(0); all waits have elapsed-time deadlines, alarms are cancelled, and the VTimer is stopped and deleted. The probe makes no absolute-time claim.
tests.risk: medium; one user-mode VTimer and six alarms, bounded waits, cancel/delete cleanup
tests.reset: one PRX launch; PSPLink soft reset before the next launch
